LESSON: ATTENTIVE LISTENING: SIMPLE INSTRUCTIONS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.3: Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you improve your listening skills?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. pronounce words from given context accurately,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. respond to instructions related to the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in pronouncing Arabic words correctly.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. pronounce words from given context accurately,

   Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. respond to instructions related to the theme for comprehension,

   Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop interest in pronouncing Arabic words correctly.

   Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

1. participate in conversations related to the facilities in the school surrounding,

2. listen attentively to an audio recording on words with nunation (Tanween),

3. work jointly to practice pronouncing the target words correctly,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. participate in conversations related to the facilities in the school surrounding,
2. listen attentively to an audio recording on words with nunation (Tanween),
3. work jointly to practice pronouncing the target words correctly,
4. answer questions related to care of school property,
5. team up to prepare class rules and instructions on

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Attentive Listening: Simple Instructions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner engages actively when holding conversations related to

the facilities in the school surrounding.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores views when preparing class rules and

instructions on how to take care of school property.

Values:
Social Justice: This is promoted as the learner accords each person an opportunity to share their views during the conversation

on facilities in the school surrounding.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: This is addressed as the learner interacts with information on facilities within their school

environment and how to care for them.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of pronunciation to their learning of similar concepts in Kiswahili.
